queue.reason: Validation early-return in pure logic (inList), not at an I/O boundary. No AC or test sends a word longer than 32 bytes next to an apostrophe, so nothing executes this path. It exists only in case such a word turns up.
queue.riskIfWrong: Deleting it alone makes normalize write past the 32-byte stack buffer when a word of 33 or more bytes sits next to an apostrophe (for example "'" followed by a long word). That is a safety-checked panic, which breaks the totality AC-F1 promises. If it is removed, the guard has to be replaced, for example by comparing word.len against the longest list entry (10, "ndrangheta"), not just deleted.

queue.reason: In lookupKeys, this condition skips combining accents when tracking the previous character. No AC-8 or AC-10 input has a combining accent before an inner apostrophe (all inputs are precomposed), so the false branch never runs. It exists 'in case'. The Dart copy in build.zig (r[i] < 0x300 || r[i] > 0x36f) mirrors it.
queue.riskIfWrong: For a word like "ĺ'aria" (letter + combining accent + apostrophe), lookupKeys would not find the inner apostrophe and would give no tail keys. The word rule treats the accent as part of the letter, so split and lookupKeys would disagree. If it is deleted, the Dart copy must go in the same change, or AC-10 parity breaks for such inputs.
